questions.stem: Con la pista «Spot an ad that uses fear to sell / Notice the emotional trigger and missing evidence. / An advertisement and its target audience», ¿qué opción se ajusta realmente al fragmento?

options.text: It uses fear to prompt action
It offers a discount
It cites a study
It targets experts only

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: the ad stokes fear of burst pipes to drive calls without evidence. On that basis "It uses fear to prompt action" is the supported choice. Option B ("It offers a discount") fails because it invents a price incentive; Option C ("It cites a study") fails because it confuses assertion with evidence; Option D ("It targets experts only") fails because it misreads the broad appeal.
questions.hint: Notice the emotional trigger and missing evidence.

questions.topic: A social media post and the brevity it imposes
questions.learningObjective: Recognise when brevity hides a limitation

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. « 100% uptime this month » Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Con «Recognise when brevity hides a limitation / Ask what 'uptime' excludes. / A social media post and the brevity it imposes» presente, ¿qué respuesta se desprende de la nota?

options.text: The maintenance window is excluded
The service has no users
Uptime is always 100%
The post is too boastful
options.misconception: judges tone, not the hidden caveat

questions.explanation: Scheduled maintenance is typically excluded from uptime figures, so '100% uptime' hides that window. Users, always-100 and tone are not the hidden caveat.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: A headline and what it foregrounds
questions.learningObjective: Spot a headline that implies causation

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: « Ice cream sales and drowning deaths both rise in July » La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Aplicando «Spot a headline that implies causation / Correlation is not causation. / A headline and what it foregrounds» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

options.text: Inferring that ice cream causes drowning
Assuming the data are fabricated
Ignoring the month of July
options.misconception: focuses on a detail, not the trap

options.text: Concluding the headline is false

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: correlation in the same month does not imply causation. On that basis "Inferring that ice cream causes drowning" is the supported choice. Option B ("Assuming the data are fabricated") fails because it jumps to fabrication; Option C ("Ignoring the month of July") fails because it focuses on a detail, not the trap; Option D ("Concluding the headline is false") fails because it misreads correlation as falsity.
questions.hint: Correlation is not causation.
